sentences.text: Ontario public health authorities recommended that the Government of Ontario should make all indoor public places 100% smoke-free, with facilities used for recreation by young people, such as arenas, bowling alleys and shopping malls, made smoke-free immediately, and target dates and specifications for other public facilities set using a phased-in approach.

The Government of Ontario should ban smoking in all enclosed worksites in the province, except where such worksites contain smoking areas which are separately-enclosed and separately-ventilated to the exterior of the premises, with implementation in stages beginning at once with office and industrial worksites, then moving to restaurants and other hospitality venues.
The Government of Ontario should fund communities to prepare and implement community-wide education programs to support smoking prevention programs delivered through the school curriculum.

The Ontario Tobacco Strategy had three overall goals: prevention of tobacco use by non-smokers, particularly children and adolescents, protection of Ontarians from second-hand smoke, and helping smokers quit.

The original objectives of the Ontario Tobacco Strategy concerned making all schools, workplaces, and public places smoke-free, eliminating sales to minors, reducing overall tobacco sales, achieving substantial reductions in the proportions of young people and adults who smoke, and eliminating the use of tobacco products by pregnant women.
